quest.title: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence
quest.description: During the Fontinalia Festival, children carry baskets and head up and down the streets asking for candies. As you roam the vibrant festive streets, you might just meet some familiar faces...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: ...Seriously!? But Mr. Morris, I don't understand, sir! How can you only be telling me this now!?

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm afraid that there's really nothing I can do. I'm really facing a crisis, my hands are tied!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: But what about my film!?

dialogues.speaker: Morris
dialogues.text: Well... I'm afraid you'll have to come up with something on your own. Take it from me, sometimes you just have to let things go. The same goes for this film festival...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, isn't that Xavier? So he's back in Fontaine now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xavier!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Ooh! Why, if it isn't the dear {NICKNAME} and Paimon! I really didn't expect to bump into you here at this time...

choices.text: It's been a while.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Well, I was doing just fine... until I received some terrible news just now. The investor I was working with for my upcoming film has fallen upon some hard times, and is no longer able to provide the promised amount of funds...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can't you just find a different investor?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Unfortunately, that's not how it works... We had signed an agreement specific to the Fontinalia Film Festival, stipulating that I cannot work with any other investors until the festival has finished.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Fontinalia Film Festival? What's that?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Oh, is this your first time participating in Fontaine's Fontinalia Film Festival? Then allow me to fill you in.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The Fontinalia Festival was established to commemorate the legendary Lochknights who went on a quest to search for the Oceanids, and eventually welcomed the Hydro Archon Egeria.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The holiday is deeply connected to the founding of Fontaine as well as its unique laws and trials. It's one of the most important festivals for this nation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what's with that weird expression on your face? It's like you're trying really hard to remember something...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah, I was just trying to recall the exact description from the books. In order to avoid any... uh, unnecessary arguments over semantics, I usually try to recite things straight from the source.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, either way, Paimon thinks she gets it now! It's just like the Windblume Festival in Mondstadt and the Lantern Rite in Liyue!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Yes, those are festivals of a similar variety! Who doesn't like a good festival? And just like those of other nations, Fontaine will hold a plethora of events around this time each year.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: To commemorate the Lochknights, people will imitate them by putting on special costumes, raising golden cups, and going door to door asking for pure water.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But a few years ago, Lady Furina started to find the whole idea a little drab, and so decided to change the part about pure water to sweets.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That really doesn't surprise Paimon at all...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The whole thing seems more akin to a carnival now, and it's quite popular among the kids. Every year, you can hear a bunch of them saying, "Trial or treat!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that sounds pretty fun! But how does that connect back to the Film Festival you mentioned?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah yes, it appears I've strayed off-topic... I just got too excited after seeing you. Let me get back to the point.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The Fontinalia Film Festival is an event proposed by the Fontaine Film Association this year. Now that film technology has matured as a medium, it's the perfect time to introduce more people to the art form.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: During this time, people may submit films to be evaluated, and the entry with the highest score will be given the "Furina Award" by the association.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The what award?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The Furina Award. You know, after the Hydro Archon? They coined it while Lady Furina was still in power, but uh... Even though things have changed, no one has made any motion to update the name.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Perhaps everyone still thinks of it as a pretty appropriate name. Even though she isn't the Hydro Archon any longer, Lady Furina is still Fontaine's superstar. Anyone with eyes can see the way she shines on the stage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, alright... Guess the name does work pretty well when you put it that way...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: *sigh* But who would've guessed there would be an issue with the funding... How will I ever explain this to Miss Chiori, not to say all the other actors who traveled all the way here from Inazuma?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chiori? Sounds familiar... Where have we heard that name before?

choices.text: She runs the clothing store in the Court of Fontaine...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Yes, that's her! I asked her to oversee the event's art direction, including the design of the actors' costumes and appearances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon remembers now! Navia said that her clothes were designed by Chiori! And Kirara's outfit, too!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: How to describe her... Uh, well, she tends to be pretty direct, and can be very forceful when it comes to dealing with people. The fashion world in Fontaine has dubbed her "The Thundering Seamstress."

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Her remarkable designs have led many Fontainians to become very interested in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Anyway, Chiori is acquainted with all the actors I've invited from Inazuma. Without her help, I don't think I would have been able to get such an international cast for the film. She really is a kind soul.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who are the actors from Inazuma? Do we know them?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Why don't the two of you accompany me to the aquabus station to welcome them?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Judging from the time, the aquabus should be arriving shortly. Chiori will be waiting to meet me there as well.

choices.text: Chioriya Boutique...
How have you been?

talks.objective: Go to the square in the Court of Fontaine
Go to the main aquabus station on the Clementine Line

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Uh, Miss Chiori...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Your talk with the investor sure went fast. The aquabus hasn't even arrived yet.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh? And who are they?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Ah, allow me to introduce you. This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Pleased to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Likewise! We've heard the owner of Chioriya Boutique is a skilled seamstress, so it's a real pleasure to finally meet you in person!

choices.text: The way Navia's wardrobe comes together is really exceptional.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Why, thank you. I strove to create an outfit that matched her high social station as the Demoiselle.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: So tell me, what happened? I can tell the conversation didn't go quite as expected.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah... Well, it's like this...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Xavier explains the issue regarding the funding to Chiori.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I know! I know, Chiori, you don't have to say it. You did remind me that this investor was a little bit sketchy.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yes, there's no doubt about that.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But how could I pass it up... He offered me twice as much as the others.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: And therein lies the problem.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Yes, but just put yourself in my shoes. After obtaining such an excellent script, it's only natural that I would want to make the most of the film.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The budgets that the others had proposed were nowhere near enough. It's difficult to find someone willing to front such a large amount of Mora, so...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be sad, Xavier. We might be able to help scrounge some Mora together for you!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Thank you, Paimon. That means a lot to me. But the cost of the film is staggering... I'm afraid that any Mora we can "scrounge" together in a short amount of time won't even be able to cover the actors' fees...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We need to move on. What's happened has already happened, and there's no changing it, but now's not the time to give up.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: What? You're saying that... you have a plan?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No, that's not what I mean. I'm simply saying I wouldn't give up just yet.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: The actors I recommended aren't just after Mora, after all.

choices.text: The concept behind Kirara's outfit is really original.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Thank you. I just wanted to make sure she wouldn't always look like a cat that had been unceremoniously dropped in a bucket of paint.

talks.objective: Go to the main aquabus station on the Clementine Line
Go to the main aquabus station on the Clementine Line

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Welcome to the Court of Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ah, Chiori! You sure have changed a lot. This is the first time we've seen you since you left Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I haven't realized it's been so long. I was in such a rush when I left that I didn't even get to say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Thank you for extending the invitation, Mr. Xavier. I'm looking forward to a fruitful trip here in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: It's an honor to have the head of the Kamisato Clan visit us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So they are who you meant when you said you had actors coming from Inazuma?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: #Oh? It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow, what a coincidence! Ayaka and I were just talking about you on the way here. Are you also here for the film?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We just ran into Xavier earlier, and came over with him.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hehe, but I'm not an actress. Sir Kamisato and Lady Ayaka are the real actors here! I'm just tagging along with Ayaka to have a good time together.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought I would always get the lead role.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Er, about that... I mean, how was I supposed to contact you when I was making preparations for the film? I figured you were probably busy, and I didn't want to disturb you...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: So I could only keep you in the back of my mind while I sought other actors to play the lead roles in this film.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I had been thinking about a surprise reunion with you during our trip here... But you still managed to surprise me first.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, so you all know each other already? My, what a coincidence! What are the chances everyone could be brought together here like this?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Why don't we go to Hotel Debord and catch up over a meal? I've already made a reservation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, did you reserve two spots for us, too?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Yes, of course, of course! I'll be sure to tell the boss to serve a few more delicious dishes, just to make sure there'll be enough food.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Very well. Then please kindly lead the way, Mr. Xavier.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: You go ahead, no need to worry about us.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I hope Furina will like the gifts we prepared. Oh, and if you still think we should get something else for her, just let me know! I should be able to make some fireworks.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Wow! The buildings in Fontaine are so tall... just look at how big they are!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: And there's the fountain that Aeval mentioned earlier. It really is a magnificent sight.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: And look at that huge spinning sphere... where does it get its power? Wait a sec, could it be one of those clockwork meka we've heard so much about?

talks.objective: Go to Hotel Debord's second floor

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Mmm, so this is what food from Fontaine is like! It sure is different from what we have in Inazuma. How should I describe it? It seems like you have to go through a lot more... steps to make them. And the flavor has many layers, too!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah yes, when I first went to Inazuma, I actually thought the food there tasted a little too bland. It took some time for me to get used to it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Let's get back to the purpose of this trip for a moment, shall we? How have preparations for the film been coming along, Mr. Xavier?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well, I've already assembled most of the film crew... A lighting specialist, a prop manager, and a costume designer... I've also bought the copyrights from the novel's author.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, it's called "The Two Musketeers," right? I read the script you sent me on the way here, the story is pretty good!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Originally, I was planning to start filming as soon as Sir Kamisato and Lady Ayaka arrived in Fontaine. But, uh... I'm afraid I've run into a bit of a problem.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: It has to do with the film's investor, Mr. Morris. He suddenly informed me this morning that he's encountered some financial trouble, and will be unable to release to me the amount of funding agreed upon...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It's said that Fontaine's legal system is well-developed. If he has violated the contract, then can't you simply take him to court over the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah, well... I'm still more concerned about filming... Even if I were to take him to court, I'm afraid it would take months before the case could even be heard.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Then, is there a way we could raise funds ourselves to solve the problem?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I've considered that option, too. But, unfortunately, it's difficult to gather such a large amount of Mora on such short notice. Besides, we have to consider the Film Festival's submission deadline...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Mr. Xavier, if Ayaka and I were willing to perform for free, would that resolve the problem you are currently facing?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: What? N—No, out of the question. To have you come all this way just to act for free? ...No, no, no, that won't do.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: There's no need to worry, Mr. Xavier. My brother and I had actually intended to work for free after receiving your invitation.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Inazuma has only recently reopened its borders, and needs to strengthen its relations and cultural ties with other nations. We didn't have many collaboration projects with Fontaine in the past, so we hoped this trip would serve as a good start for the future.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Indeed, you could say that's the real reason why the Yashiro Commission agreed to come to Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I understand, but... having you two act for free just doesn't seem right.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Not at all. While we're officially here to conduct a "cultural survey" of sorts, we must express our sincerity if we want to establish formal cultural ties with your nation.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: This film will serve as proof of friendly cooperation and cultural exchange between Inazuma and Fontaine. It's my hope that the film can be finished and released as smoothly as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If you still don't feel comfortable with this arrangement, I would also be more than happy to be introduced to some other renowned individuals in Fontaine's literary and artistic circles.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll do as you say. Thank you... Thank you so much. I'll make sure to cobble together enough Mora now, even if it means selling my house, my Kamera, and every single family heirloom!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: C'mon now, no need to go that far. I'll also help you out as a brand sponsor.

choices.text: We can help, too...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Me too! Even though I didn't bring much Mora to spend on this trip... It's still better than nothing!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: You are too kind, all of you! *sniff* I... I really don't know how to...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alright, enough about that. Now that we have Xavier's savings, my support, and two leads who are willing to act for free... I think we will be able to make this happen.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: So instead of Mora, you'll help with filming and production.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, but how can we help with that? We don't know much about making a film...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alright, pull yourself together, Xavier. Tell us if there are still any open positions left among the crew.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: ...Oh, al—alright. Let me think... we still need a Kamera operator, a clapper loader, and someone to manage logistics.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I originally wanted to personally serve as director, but I've been too busy working as the producer... So, the positions of director and director's assistant will also need to be filled...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows what the director and the logistics support person do, but what's a clapper loader?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The clapper loader is responsible for using the clapperboard to record and organize the information of each shot when the Kamera operator begins shooting. The work requires both patience and careful attention to detail.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A clapperboard? Oh, you mean the thing they hold that goes CLAP whenever they start filming?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yes, that's right. Are you interested in that job?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: For sure! Paimon's always wanted to try that!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alright, then you'll be our clapper loader. I can find someone from the store to help with logistics. What do you think, Xavier?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Fine by me. As for our Kamera operator, I was thinking of letting {NICKNAME} take the role.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh, {M#he's}{F#she's} great when it comes to using a Kamera! Paimon can't even count how many things we've taken photos of during our journey.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Yes, that's also what I was thinking. I noticed {NICKNAME} had an eye for photography and composition when we worked together previously.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: #I'm sure that's due to {NICKNAME}'s journey across Teyvat and all the places they've seen. After so many adventures, using a Kamera must be second nature by now.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: What do you say, Traveler? Are you interested in the job?

choices.text: As long as I'll be able to help.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Thank you, it really means a lot to me! C'mon, friend, let me give you a big, warm hug!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh, I think we'd better get to work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So all that's left for us to find is a director and an assistant.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh! Me, me, me! I want to be the director's assistant! All I need to do is help the director, right? I can handle that!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Alright, then all we need is a director... *sigh* All the well-known directors in Fontaine are probably also busy working on their own films these days... I'm not sure who will have time to help.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Furina helped out a theater troupe recently by serving as an artistic consultant. She could be a good director, right? Besides, it's not like she has anything else to do right now...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: F—Furina?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Uh, do you really think Lady Furina would be willing to help us with our humble project?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Isn't that the name of Fontaine's Hydro Archon? My brother has already informed me about what happened here in Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's her! She helped out a theater troupe not too long ago, and now she's taking up work as a director.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Well, uh...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Ah, I saw that musical. Her performance was perfect, and the storyboards were also excellent.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Don't let her former identity intimidate you. She's the best candidate we can think of right now. You'll never know until you give her a shot.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Fine... You're right, Chiori. I'll do anything for the sake of my film... anything!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Whew... Then I'll have to ask {NICKNAME} and Paimon to show me the way to Lady Furina's residence. I just hope she'll agree to help.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Do you need us to also come along?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: No, there's no need to trouble you with this. Besides, you've just arrived in Fontaine, and I'm sure there are many places you would like to visit.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Just leave this task to me... It's part of my duties as the producer.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Very well, then we'll be waiting to hear the good news.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I'll go with you. By the way, you might want to consider bringing a gift.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And don't worry, we won't simply drop you off at Furina's place! We know Furina pretty well by now, so having some familiar faces there should help your chances... Besides, the whole thing was our idea in the first place!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Alright, then I'll start making preparations. As for the gift...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hmm, a gift for someone who was once seen as the Hydro Archon. I wonder what she would like...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I recall that Lady Furina once fancied a clockwork ring, so perhaps I should get another exquisite clockwork contraption for her?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Huh? Can't we just bring some desserts? Like the Fontinalia Mousse?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, but wouldn't that be a little too cheap? She does like desserts though...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Isn't the Fontinalia Festival happening right now? I heard Aeval tell us on the aquabus that Furina introduced the tradition of going door-to-door and asking for sweets.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: To do something like that... she must have a real sweet tooth.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I agree with Yoimiya. If the gift is too fancy, it might actually make her feel more uncomfortable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then! Let's go buy some Fontinalia Mousse!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But will that really be enough? We'll be asking her to do a lot of work, you know.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm, you're right. We need to further sweeten the deal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You want something even sweeter than Fontinalia Mousse?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yes, we'll need a gift that's sweeter than any dessert in the world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what could that be?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Your words of praise.

choices.text: Lights, Kamera, action!
Just say that you got our contribution from some personal friends.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here, this is where Furina lives.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Okay, I'll go knock on the door.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *yawn* Coming, coming... Seriously, who's knocking before afternoon tea...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Lady Furina, please allow me to introduce myself. I am Xavier, a film director.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Hello. Oh? Is that {NICKNAME} and Paimon I see behind you? And who's this...?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I'm Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ah, the one from Chioriya Boutique! Hello, hello.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So what are you all doing here? Do you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you just get up, Furina? It's already past noon, you know...

choices.text: Ahem... Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, uh... Paimon means the weather is so nice in the afternoon, and the sun so warm, just like how you make us feel! Sleeping in late is a really smart idea!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Ah, no... I was just up late last night reading some novels... What does sleeping in have to do with the weather?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ahem, this is a small gift we prepared for you, Lady Furina. We hope you'll like it.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: No need to be so formal, I'm just a regular person like everyone else now. Oh! Is this Fontinalia Mousse? It's one of my favorites!

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: That's great! So, actually, there's something we need your help with...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Given your renowned passion and understanding of drama, I would like to ask you to serve as the director of our film crew.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Huh? But didn't you just say that you're a director?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Yes, but for this particular project, I'm mainly working as a producer. Besides, I'm sure that your understanding of the performing arts far surpasses my own, Lady Furina.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #Are {NICKNAME} and Paimon also part of the film crew?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Yep, we sure are! Paimon's the clapper loader and {M#he's}{F#she's} the Kamera operator.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Kamera operator? That can be a pretty technical job, and it directly affects the final quality of the film. Are you really up to it?

choices.text: I have experience.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: No, I'm not questioning your abilities. It's just that, I've never really seen you use a Kamera before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Maybe you can come up with a test for {NICKNAME} and see for yourself!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #If {M#he}{F#she} can satisfy you with {M#his}{F#her} Kamera skills, then you'd have nothing to worry about and can join the team. Whaddya say?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: #Uh, you sure are getting better at rolling with the situation, Paimon. Hmm, I do wish to see how skilled {NICKNAME} really is with a Kamera.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Alright, how about this... We'll work with what we have. I'll give you some scenarios, and see if your work is up to my standards.

choices.text: Sure, no problem.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Very good. It's essential for the Kamera operator to understand the director's vision. I'll make my decision after seeing your work.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Are you ready? I have high standards, you know.

choices.text: Yep, I'm ready.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Okay. Grab the Kamera, and I'll give you a scenario.

choices.text: Please wait a moment.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Sure. You can come back once you've reviewed the basics of film composition and feel ready.

choices.text: Whatever you say, Director Furina.
I can show you if you like.
Try to be nice, remember?

talks.objective: Complete the theme Furina is directing
Complete the theme Furina is directing

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Let me be honest... Do you really think you have what it takes to shoot a film?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You put no thought into finding a good Kamera angle, and the characters weren't even in the shots. As for the original intent of the characters' lines... did you leave them somewhere in the vicinity of Elton Trench?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I mean, I guess you could be trying to pursue your definition of the avant-garde... if that's what you're doing, I suppose you do have to find yourselves a capable director...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what's the verdict?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, does that mean you agree to be our director, Furina?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hah, did you think I would agree just like that? After our performance of "The Little Oceanid," I've begun to make a name for myself again, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: In fact, I've already had several troupes approach me for the Fontinalia Film Festival. Unfortunately, the scripts were all pretty boring, and didn't pique my interest.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If others were to find out I agreed to work with you so easily, then, well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, but didn't we have a deal? What else do we need to do to convince you, Furina?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh... Well, what about the pay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You know... how much you're willing to pay me to be the director? The pay is also an important factor for me to consider, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Well, uh... I can offer you... this much...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...What? That's all!? If Neuvillette were to hear of this, he could charge you with underpaying your labor!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but our crew is in a tight financial spot at the moment...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I see. Well, even though it's highly unlikely now that I'll join your crew, there's still something I'd like to ask... Exactly what film are you planning to make?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Our script is an adaption of "The Two Musketeers."

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, you mean the suspense thriller novel that was a number-one bestseller?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so Furina's read it, too!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course I've read it! I've always had a keen interest in artistic works that strike a chord with the populace.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I see... It all makes sense now. You must've used most of the budget to pay for the copyright.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Uh, not really... The novel's author transferred the copyright to me practically for free once he heard that I wanted to make a film adaption of the story. The lack of budget is due to another issue...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: He probably just wants to get his name out there, so Mora isn't the most important thing to him right now.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It reminds me of a delivery courier who wears one of my designs while traveling all across Teyvat. I didn't charge her much for the outfit, either. The exposure she provides for my brand is well worth it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, are you a big fan of this story, Furina?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, uh... it's alright! The pacing of the story is good, but the character relationships could use some work. When I was reading it before, I always felt like some things were left on a rather unsatisfactory note. I have high standards, you know!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Ahem... Mr. Xavier, if, hypothetically speaking, I agree to be the director... how much freedom would I have in terms of script revisions and creative interpretation?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, as much freedom as you would need! I wouldn't dare doubt the tastes of Fontaine's greatest star.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Good. Then I'm free to alter the script as I see fit?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Absolutely, no problem!

choices.text: We're counting on you, Director Furina.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hmm, alright. It seems that your crew really can't go on without my care and direction.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: So... you agree?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Yes, I agree. Although the pay is well below what someone of my caliber deserves, a great script calls for a great director.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I mustn't let a perfectly good story be ruined due to lack of funds. If you have fine cheese and bread, you wouldn't let it just sit on the counter and get moldy just because you lack an oven, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you, Furina.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Oh, Hydro Archon above... I'm not dreaming, am I? Somebody pinch me.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: There's no more Hydro Archon, you know... And it's still a little early to celebrate.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: There's a lot that goes into shooting a film. Although the trickiest tasks of finalizing the script and casting the actors have already been taken care of, we'll still need to reserve filming locations, not to say set up lighting and props...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: And by the way, since we'll be filming "The Two Musketeers," we'll need to find an action choreographer... Ideally, a professional who has actual experience with muskets.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Yes, I've thought about this as well. I was hoping that you might know someone who could handle the job.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Me? Hmm... if this was before, I could have simply asked Clorinde. But it's already been some time since I last talked to her.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Navia can also use firearms, but unfortunately, her style is quite different from that of the characters in the story.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Could we ask the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Oh, you mean the Special Patrol's Musketeers?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yes, that's right. They work with muskets every day. I can't think of anyone more qualified than them.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: They would be under Neuvillette's jurisdiction. Unfortunately, I uh... Don't have any connection with them at all.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hmm, so... in the end, we still have to start by talking to Neuvillette...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No need to go to all that trouble. I know their captain, Chevreuse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you do? Wait, Chiori, how do you know the captain of the Special Patrol's Musketeers?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No particular reason. Running a business means dealing with some trouble from time to time, and she's helped me out on a few occasions.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: In return, I've helped her handle a few situations in which the Special Patrol couldn't get involved directly. So, we've gotten to know each other over time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, so you're saying there's been times when the Special Patrol needed a fashion designer to handle a situation? Your work is becoming more and more mysterious...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: It'd be best to keep it that way. Anyway, enough about that. What do you all think about asking the captain to be our musket action choreographer?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: She sounds professional enough. She is a captain, after all. I have no objections.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: But I imagine the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol must be busy with their duties. Do you think she'd really have time to help with shooting a film? And then there's the issue of pay...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, it just so happens that she's also not the kind of person that's just after Mora. As for whether she has time, I'll have to go and ask her first.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Then I'll leave that to you. Macaroni's on sale today, so I've got to go. You can just tell me how things went when we discuss tomorrow's plan later.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: No problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeee! Having Furina join feels like a big boost to our team.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Of course, just wait until the day of our premiere. You'll witness the true power of my name in these lands! You'll be so glad I agreed to help. I can guarantee that even the standing tickets will be sold out.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'll be sure to ask some people I know to see if they'd be willing to act as extras.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ha, seems like you're finally getting more comfortable with your own reputation now!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I didn't ask for the clapper loader's commentary, Paimon.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't wait to see our film's premiere.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Then let's get going. I happen to know where Chevreuse is today.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: By the way, I'm curious. If my pay is so low, then what about our two lead actors? Didn't they travel here all the way from Inazuma?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Actually, they told us that they see the trip as a part of cultural exchange... So they didn't ask for any pay.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What? So is every person in Teyvat who doesn't want money gathered here to shoot this film? Don't tell me Chiori isn't being paid either...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I already knew Xavier from before, and he's also agreed to give my brand some good exposure.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: It seems the gods have really smiled upon you, Xavier... And that certainly doesn't include me, mind you.

choices.text: Now's your chance to make a film that you love.

talks.objective: Look for Chevreuse, Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Alright, this is the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm? But where's the captain? There's hardly anyone around here.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: She's over there... The one with an eye patch reading in front of the newsstand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, her! Paimon could tell there was something different about her. She seems kinda intimidating!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Please wait here for a moment, I'll go fetch her. She's working now, so you might not want to get in her way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Working? But isn't she just standing there and reading a novel?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Just trust me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... alright. Let's see what happens then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori sure is a mysterious person... She claims just to be a fashion designer, but she knows all these powerful people.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The Court of Fontaine isn't particularly tolerant of visitors from overseas, so it isn't easy for a foreigner to promote their brand here... Even more so in the competitive world of fashion.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Even a local like me just trying to make a film has to face all kinds of challenges, so I can only imagine what Chiori has been through to get to where she is today. I'm sure that having more connections has definitely worked in her favor.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Reading on the job?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Detective novel.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: One main character?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: No, multiple. Branching storylines.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I see. How's the plot coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: One of the main characters is about to make a choice that will affect the rest of his life. I'd wager he's going to make the wrong choice.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Any way to speed things up? There's something I need your help with.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: You know that doesn't depend on me. It all comes down to what the character chooses.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Which is exactly why I'm here to help.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Alright. It appears he made the wrong choice in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Halt!

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Owner
dialogues.text: Huh!? Wh—What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hand over whatever you're holding.

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Customer
dialogues.text: Oh, it's just a book. I didn't buy anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Then I'm sure you wouldn't mind letting me have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Owner
dialogues.text: Excuse me, officer. I don't mind you standing around here and not purchasing anything, but I'd prefer if you didn't disturb my customers. It's bad for business, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Don't give me that act. You won't be able to get off so easily, either.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: I am Chevreuse, Captain of Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. I will say this one last time — hand over whatever you're holding at once.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And before you do anything unwise, let me remind you that I'll have you on the ground before you can even think about making a run for it.

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Customer
dialogues.text: Ah! Alright, alright, I'll give it to you!

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Customer
dialogues.text: B—But, please let me say something first! If there's any contraband in that book, then the shopkeeper here is the one who slipped it in. I don't have anything to do with this!

dialogues.speaker: Book Stall Owner
dialogues.text: Why, you! Trying to leave me on the hook, huh? You were the one who said you wanted it...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Save it for the interrogation room.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Take them away, Letellier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on here? One second you're reading a book, the next you're escorting people away!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: And who are... Oh? Aren't you the Traveler who's been all over the papers recently? Chiori, I'm assuming what you wanted to ask me about has to do with them, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Eh, maybe I can let you in on what's happening then.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Now that Vacher has been brought to justice, no new shipments of Sinthe will be made and distributed to sellers. The Fontaine Gardes have been busy collecting the remaining Sinthe still circulating on the market.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Thanks to a tip from our reliable source here, this should be the very last batch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you were pretending to read a book in order to catch the bad guys...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, Paimon almost forgot to introduce ourselves! Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME} and Xavier.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hey, I'm Chevreuse. You probably already heard me introduce myself, so I won't bother repeating it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why didn't you just arrest them immediately?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yeah, why didn't you make a move as soon as you had the chance? Were you worried that my intel wasn't accurate?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: No, I wanted to see if the shopkeeper would turn himself in first.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: All he had to do was come up to me and say that he didn't know where the Sinthe had come from. If he did that, then I wouldn't have had to press charges on him.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: He had the whole day to turn the Sinthe over to Chevreuse. But instead, the moment I came up and blocked Chevreuse's line of sight, he took the opportunity to sell it off.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, he made the wrong choice, even though the right choice was right there in front of him.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: But you knew they wouldn't make the right choice.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yeah, I knew. I was just hoping I'd be wrong for once.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Enough about that, though. What did you want to ask me about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you see, it's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain to Chevreuse your plans to make the film...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: "The Two Musketeers"... You certainly have a good eye for a story.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: So what do you need me to do? Just be the action choreographer for the actors?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. I want to make sure we get all the details right... I want the actors' posture and understanding of firearms to be as realistic as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: However, I'm afraid this work will require quite a bit of your time, since you'll have to be present whenever we are filming... Also, as for the pay...

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: No need to say any more. I'll join.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Just like that!?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: R—Really? You're willing to help us with our humble film project?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Sure, it's no big deal. As I said, we've wrapped up our investigation here, so I don't have any other tasks on my plate for the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Besides, I personally really like this novel. I even have the collector's edition at home. Stories where justice prevails over evil never get old for me.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Then we've got a deal?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yes, I'll see you on-set tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh my... I can hardly believe it! I should tell Lady Furina immediately. Oh, and I must tell the prop manager and lighting technician to get everything ready. We start filming tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Calm down, Xavier. The film is going to take more than just a day to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Still, I should also head back now and start preparing the actors' costumes and make-up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, guess that's it for today then.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, please stay for a moment. I have something to tell you.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Then I'll take Xavier back. Poor thing, he's so excited that he can't even walk straight anymore. I don't want to spend our first day fishing our producer out of the fountain.

choices.text: See you tomorrow!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yep, see you tomorrow.

choices.text: I think Xavier would probably be able to hold himself together.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: He'd better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what did you want to tell us, Chevreuse?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Have you read "The Two Musketeers"?

choices.text: I've heard a bit about it.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The story is about a pair of children born into the household of a baron, and their struggle to survive together and take revenge for their mother.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: They were raised at the baron's estate, where their mother worked as a maid. The two were illegitimate children that the baron had with the maid, so they were never treated well by anyone.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: One day, upon returning home, they found their mother had been murdered and left dead on the floor. It was quite evident that the culprits were the other members of the baron's household, who never had any kind words to say to them.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: However, the baron was able to exert his influence and keep the whole thing under wraps. The mother's death was eventually deemed as a suicide, and there was no chance of bringing her murderers to justice. The two siblings decided to flee and someday avenge their mother.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Many years later, members of the baron's family suddenly started turning up dead one after the other... all killed by gunshot. A Rainbow Rose was found on each of the victim's bodies, being the flower that the kids' mother liked best.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The baron believed that the mother's soul had come to take vengeance on him, so he lived in fear each day.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: But it was actually those two siblings who had fled all those years ago. They relied on each other to survive and trained day and night, eventually becoming adept musketeers.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: They used all of their abilities to collect evidence and clues, before executing their plan and exacting revenge on the baron. Their actions let the truth behind their mother's death be known to all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's quite an exhilarating story!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Yep, the baron got what he deserved for his evil deeds, and justice was able to prevail. It was just the kind of story I enjoy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so is that why you were so willing to join our crew, Chevreuse?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: You could say it was one of the reasons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? You mean there were other reasons, too?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I've read the reports about you. Whether it was at the trials, or when you lent your hand to resolve our nation's crisis...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: You've shown that you've got a strong sense of justice, as well as a great mind for deductions.

choices.text: Wait, so what you're implying is...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Yes, you're as sharp as I expected. It seems you've experienced many similar situations before.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: There's been a recent murder case involving muskets. The perpetrator's methods appear to be very similar to what is described in the novel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Really!? But Paimon didn't see anything about that in today's papers.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: The Marechaussee Phantom hasn't yet released any information to the public, because the investigation is currently at a standstill. The murderer is extremely cautious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A murder involving firearms... But not that many people use those in Fontaine, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could it be someone from your platoon?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Impossible. We perform a routine inspection of our firearms and ammo reserves every day. If one of the weapons had been fired, it would stick out like a sore thumb. Besides, I trust the members of my platoon.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: However... Well, that's all I can disclose about the case today.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Whaddya mean?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I hope you all can go back and get some shut-eye. You can decide tomorrow whether or not you'd like to join the investigation with me.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'm aware this might not be the ideal time to add more to your plate, but the more capable people we have, the better the chances that justice will prevail.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Can't someone from the Special Patrol help you investigate?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Carrying out investigations isn't actually supposed to be our responsibility. Our job is to apprehend the perpetrators... finding them is really up to the Marechaussee Phantom. You could say I'm taking part in the investigation out of personal interest.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I don't want people to see muskets in a negative way, and also... I'm concerned about the similarity between the crimes and the story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean... they might be connected somehow?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I suspect so.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Just to make myself clear, this is not an order, nor is it a deal of any kind. It's a request, nothing more.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: If you two have any interest in the case after we finish filming tomorrow, and are willing to assist me, then I would be most grateful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, what do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It's already been quite a day...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. Paimon's getting a little tired, too. We've really been hustling all day.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: You'd better head back and get some rest. It's good to keep a calm mind, especially when you're about to make an important decision.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Otherwise, when the moment comes, you might end up like that shopkeeper, and not even realize that the right choice is right there in front of you.

choices.text: Let's give it some thought tomorrow.
There's a case that you need our help with?
I haven't read it yet.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh? It appears that you have more skill than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: All the shots had great composition, and I could really feel a connection to the characters and their lines...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: ...Really!? Then where do you live?

dialogues.speaker: Aeval
dialogues.text: We Melusines live in Merusea Village. The only way to enter is from underwater!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Whoa, then you must be pretty tired after work every day, right? I mean, you have to swim all that way just to go home.

dialogues.speaker: Aeval
dialogues.text: You're so thoughtful! But some Melusines choose to live in the Court of Fontaine because it's so much more convenient.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: This is our stop.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh? We've arrived? But I haven't even finished chatting with Aeval yet!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I also enjoyed Aeval's introductions to Fontaine along the way. Everything you described was so clear and detailed that we can't help but want to hear more.

dialogues.speaker: Aeval
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! I'm usually working here on this aquabus, so I hope I'll have the chance to see you again. There are still many more places I'd like to introduce to you.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Looking forward to the good news.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Besides the macaroni, I should also pick up some tomato sauce...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, have you seen The Steambird? It seems Fontaine has been celebrating some kind of festival recently. Things are looking pretty lively in the square, they even changed the banners!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there are a lot of people holding Kameras... Oh, and they've got candy and snacks, too! Looks like everyone's having a good time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go have a look for ourselves!
